patterns: INVALIDATION LEVELS ARE SET BUT NEVER ENFORCED. MSFT's 5/19 entry set 'stock closes below $400' as its stop; MSFT closed below $400 on 6/10 and fell to $352 by 6/25 without a single session flagging the breach. A second, self-imposed trigger set on 6/17 ('$380 break-below = trim') was breached on 6/24-6/25 and also never acted on. This is the single most concrete, fixable failure in the whole history: research is genuinely updated with fresh data every session, but the stated triggers from prior sessions are never checked against current price before deciding to hold again.

Catalyst-anticipation trades lose money twice in the same way: AAPL was built up over two weeks purely ahead of WWDC on Street-high analyst targets, then closed at a loss when the event disappointed (-4.4%). XLE was bought on an Iran/Hormuz war-shock narrative and invalidated within 6 days by IEA demand data (-5.2%). Both are 'buy the well-telegraphed catalyst, thesis already priced in, event undershoots' failures.

Whipsaw churn between QQQ and AAPL: bought 1 QQQ (5/28), sold it 6 days later to fund more AAPL (6/3), then closed all of AAPL and bought QQQ again (6/16) -- three moves between the same two vehicles in three weeks, netting a modest loss overall once the AAPL leg is included.

Concentration risk was well-managed early (NVDA trimmed from ~45% to ~34% of equity across two sessions in late May) but that discipline was never reapplied after 6/2, even as new fundamental risks emerged on both MSFT (capex/FCF compression) and NVDA (China market exit) through June.

The single unmanaged, un-researched position (SPY, held flat for 45 sessions) outperformed every actively-managed name and the whole book. The portfolio's entire active management layer has subtracted value relative to just holding the passive core.
suggested_adjustments: Make invalidation checks mechanical, not narrative: every session must explicitly compare current price to any invalidation/trigger level set in a prior session for each open position, and if breached, the default action is trim/close -- not a fresh 'thesis still intact' paragraph. This alone would have caught both MSFT breaches.
If a position is down >15% from entry AND has breached its own stated trigger, require an actual size reduction before the position is allowed to just 'hold' again in the next session.

Discount well-telegraphed catalysts (WWDC, COMPUTEX, earnings) that are already reflected in raised analyst price targets going into the event -- require the outcome to beat the re-priced expectation, not just occur, before sizing into it. This would have blocked the AAPL WWDC add.

Stop rotating capital between overlapping vehicles (QQQ vs. direct mega-cap names) to fund a different conviction trade -- pick single-name or broad-ETF exposure per thesis and hold it, rather than swapping mid-stream.

graded_decisions.news_since: Two proactive, non-stop-triggered trims this window: 07-20 cut 15->11.4 sh into a chip-sector relief rally to finally hit the review-mandated <=25%-of-equity cap (first time since May); 07-28 cut again (11.4->5.7 sh @ $193.42) on WSJ reporting (7/26-27) that Nvidia is negotiating a ~$250B OpenAI Ohio data-center financing guarantee plus ~$350B chip-purchase financing, which spiked Nvidia's 5yr CDS spread to a record ~82bp and triggered a KOSPI circuit-breaker/Nikkei -4%+ global chip selloff. graded_decisions.comment: Both trims were genuinely proactive (ahead of any stop breach) rather than reactive, directly answering three straight prior reviews' complaint that concentration risk was flagged but never acted on. NVDA is now ~12% of equity (down from ~32% in mid-July), and the risk that triggered the second trim (circular AI financing) is confirmed real and still unresolved, not a false alarm -- the trim looks well-timed given the stock has only round-tripped back to ~$197.5, not staged a strong recovery. Aug 26 earnings remains the next real catalyst; $190 hard stop stays mechanical.

graded_decisions.news_since: Entered on a confirmed Brent spike to $94-100/bbl (Iran/Hormuz tanker strikes) after 5 prior sessions had declined the trade for lack of confirmation. Exited 4 days later on reports of a US-Iran hostilities pause. Follow-up research shows that pause did NOT hold -- Iran fired missiles at US forces and the US resumed strikes 7/28-29, and Strait shipping traffic stayed near-empty (<10 vessels/day vs ~100 normal) even during the 'pause.' So the exit's stated rationale (de-escalation) was itself wrong within 48 hours.
graded_decisions.comment: Net effect was still a small loss (-2.5%) rather than a bigger one, because XLE/energy equities didn't rally proportionally when oil re-spiked to ~$90 on the renewed strikes -- so the whipsaw call, though factually wrong, wasn't costly. This is the second Iran/oil-narrative round-trip in this book's history (after the 5/21-5/27 XLE loss flagged in the first weekly review) and the second loss -- 0-for-2 on geopolitical-oil entries. The entry itself also chased a move already +13% over 3 weeks rather than catching it early.

QQQ's 7/17 stop remains the one case where the stop clearly avoided further downside. The pattern across three enforced stops is now 1-for-3 clearly vindicated, 2-for-3 modest whipsaws -- still probably worth the tail-risk protection, but the cost is real and recurring, not zero.

graded_decisions.news_since: Re-entered after the FY26 Q4 print (7/29, after close) confirmed a genuine beat -- revenue $90.01B (+18% YoY) vs $87.6B consensus, EPS $4.81, Azure crossed $100B annualized at 43% YoY growth -- and the resulting ~15.6% one-day gap (confirmed as the largest single-day market-cap gain in US stock market history, ~$450B added) held and extended for a second session through 7/31. FY2027 capex guidance of $255-260B (+35% YoY) is a live, credible margin/ROI risk still being debated by sell-side, not resolved.
graded_decisions.comment: This is the exact re-entry test the desk set for itself on 7/10 (wait for the actual print, then require the gap to hold 2+ sessions before chasing) executed correctly -- avoided both the pre-earnings preview trap and the same-day FOMO-into-a-gap mistake. Position is under a day old so grading the trade itself is premature, but the underlying thesis is validated so far and the stated $430 invalidation level gives real room before the next mechanical check matters.

patterns: Concentration-risk discipline finally became proactive, not just reactive: NVDA was trimmed twice this window purely on sizing/risk grounds (07-20 into a rally, 07-28 on a fresh unresolved risk) rather than waiting for a hard-stop breach -- a first in this book's history and a direct, executed response to three consecutive prior reviews' top complaint.

Earnings discipline (wait for the actual print, don't trade the preview or the same-day gap) had its best week yet: it correctly kept the desk out of AAPL's post-earnings drop (stock fell ~9.4% on weak guidance despite a headline beat -- the desk read the real numbers and skipped) and correctly gated the MSFT re-entry until the gap had confirmed for 2 sessions. Both were graded 'process wins' with no exceptions this window.

Mechanical stop-outs are now 1-for-3 clearly vindicated (QQQ 7/17) and 2-for-3 modest whipsaws (MSFT 7/10, SPY 7/30) -- both of the whipsaw cases saw the price rebound above the stop level within 1-2 sessions of the exit. The discipline is still worth keeping (it avoided real downside on QQQ and capped the tail on the other two), but the account should track this cost explicitly rather than treating every enforced stop as an unqualified win.

Geopolitical/oil single-name trades remain a clean 0-for-2 in this book: the historical XLE entry (5/21-5/27, -5.16%) and this week's XLE round-trip (7/23-27, -2.51%) both lost money, and this week's exit rationale (a 'ceasefire') was itself proven wrong within 48 hours by the conflict re-escalating. The desk has not yet found a reliable way to trade this catalyst.

The account is now sitting ~78% in cash (long market value $2,033 of $9,244 equity) with only NVDA and MSFT held -- both SPY and XLE were closed this window and no re-entry signal has fired for SPY, right as SPY/VT quietly turned positive again into 7/31. This is a reasonable defensive posture given the FOMC/earnings/Iran risk cluster this week, but it also means the book is not currently capturing any broad-market beta at all, a meaningfully different risk profile than every prior review period.
suggested_adjustments: Add an explicit 'post-stop-out rebound check': after any mechanical stop-loss close, log whether price reclaims the stop level within 2 sessions, and report the cost/benefit in the next weekly review rather than treating every enforced stop as a clean win by default -- this window alone had 2 of 3 stops give back most of their benefit within a day or two.
